key_insight: Individual tokens in diffusion language models often converge earlier than the whole sequence; a training-free, token-level early stopping rule based on lightweight signals lets the model finalize tokens independently, saving compute without retraining.
problem_solved: Diffusion text generation is computationally inefficient because many token positions stabilize well before the final denoising step and there is no effective per-token stopping mechanism.
method: Detect per-token convergence using lightweight signals derived from the model's predictions and local context (e.g., prediction consistency, local stability metrics).
Apply a dynamic, training-free stopping criterion at each diffusion step to finalize tokens and exclude them from further refinement.
Maintain full-generation quality by using conservative, context-aware thresholds while substantially reducing iterations for stable tokens.
impact: Practical way to reduce inference time, compute cost, and latency for diffusion LMs with minimal engineering and no retraining—useful for deployed generation systems and research experiments.
visual_elements: Flow diagram of diffusion generation where tokens drop out progressively as per-token stop signals trigger.
Line chart showing per-token confidence/stability over steps and the moment each token is finalized versus full-model stopping.
Bar chart comparing inference time / FLOPs between standard diffusion, sequence-level stopping, and token-level early stopping.
Icon set: token symbol + stop flag, clock/speedometer for latency, and a shield or checkmark for preserved quality.
paper_title: Just on Time: Token-Level Early Stopping for Diffusion Language Models
paper_authors: Zahar Kohut, Severyn Shykula, Dmytro Khamula, Mykola Vysotskyi, Taras Rumezhak
